_: What is said in each voice note, one line per entry. Words in [brackets] are ElevenLabs audio tags: the v3 voice acts on them and the captions leave them out. `pnpm voice` turns these into narration and timed captions; `pnpm voice 3` redoes one note.
notes: [warmly] Hey stranger... welcome to Sharn's story, in Sharn's words.
I'm Sharn, a developer from Waterloo, Ontario.
I write code for the web... and I've been doing it since before I knew it was a job.
[chuckles] My first program was a webpage with a marquee tag and a visitor counter.
It got eleven visits. [laughs] Ten were me.
Grow up curious, and everyone wants exactly one thing for you: [sighs] a sensible plan.
[softly] I had other plans.
Well... I actually have a sensible plan now. But we'll get to that.
[amused] Hear me out... building for the web was never the plan.
[earnestly] I swear.
When you start out, there are only two doors: [dryly] Java... or C++.
[sighs] I tried both.
[laughs] Yeah. Both doors.
But turns out there was a window. [warmly] It was called the browser.
[excited] Fun fact: my first real project was a to-do app, like everyone else's.
[deadpan] Most people stop at the to-do app.
I added a backend, then a login... [laughs] then a bug that logged everyone in as me.
[sheepishly] I knew nothing, and I almost shipped it.
[reflective] 8,000 lines of code, in a codebase I had only seen in screenshots.
[curious] And you know what screenshots skip?
[softly] The most important parts.
[sighs] Nobody warns you about the move from tutorials to a real repo.
[laughs] Nobody teaches you to navigate a ten-year-old migrations folder.
[exhales] Culture shock was very real.
[proudly] But I made it.
[warmly] Clean... and with tests.
[cheerfully] Like every junior on the team, I worked the support queue to fund my weekends.
[amused] Well, basically the IT desk... but for our own product.
Code was my second favourite part of the job.
[curious] You know what the first was?
[warmly] It was the customers who came in fighting with our app.
I'd fix their issue in five, [chuckles] and then we'd talk for another thirty minutes.
[sincerely] I love talking to people to solve their problems.
[proudly] Eight months in, I was running the on-call rotation... and I still took those calls.
[amused] I also noticed that nobody read our release notes.
[mischievously] But everyone read the little banner inside the app.
[excited] So you know what? I put the release notes in the banner.
We got what we needed. Best ad space on the product, [laughs] and it came with a close button.
[cheerfully] My first big project was a design system, with a team across three time zones.
[sheepishly] Well... my meeting attendance was the bare minimum,
[amused] because I was busy building, pairing with people, and getting lost in Figma files.
[playfully] You could say I was studying cross-functional communication... in the field,
[warmly] and it was totally worth it.
[dramatically] Then came the big rewrite... and the second biggest risk of my life:
[softly] a one-way migration to production.
One way because... [nervously] I don't know, a rollback plan felt like a plan.
[excited] And guess what, I discovered feature flags,
[laughs] made the best mistakes,
and moved the whole thing over... on a Friday night.
[exhales] The most terrifying time of my life.
[whispers] Well, my manager does not need to hear about this.
[cheerfully] My next role came with a side quest: mentoring interns through their first pull requests.
[amused] If you think tech leads ask hard questions,
[laughs] try a room full of interns.
[warmly] We built a small app together, and it was so much fun.
[softly] I promised my parents I'd get a stable job... and I did.
[proudly] Today I'm a full-stack developer, working on things that real people use every day.
[amused] So yes, the kid with the marquee tag now has a stable job.
[laughs] And yeah, my resume's very, very proud of me.
[curious] But remember when I said production was the second biggest risk of my life?
[softly] Well... this is the first.
[reflective] Everything the sensible plan asked for, I already have it.
[sincerely] And I'm still sending you this.
[warmly] Because what I love is building things that make people's days a little easier,
[hopeful] and I want to do that for you.
[warmly] Thank you... for the ones who actually stayed until the end.
[excited] Here you go: the source code for this site. [laughs] Pencil, cassette, tape and all.
